messages:
ali: heads-up — saw regression on prod after the kernel selector change at 3961220000. long-sequence p95 latency up ~2.1x, and a couple of tenants seeing near-starvation when cluster is saturated with short requests.
meera: ugh. is that the kernel that prioritizes fast-path for short sequences?
ali: yes. kernel v2.4 swap-in caused microbatching to favor short requests due to cheaper kernel choice + quicker kv misses. logs attached.
perf-bot: profile summary attached: cpu: kernel_v2.4 fastpath wins 72% for seq<=32, kv_miss_penalty increased 45ms avg for seq>512, kv_hit_rate drop correlated with long tail.
ryan: can you paste the relevant flamegraph snippet?
ali: pasted below:
```
flamegraph: runtime_loop -> select_kernel(v2.4) -> batch_builder -> kv_fetch_serial -> wait(45ms) -> context_switch
```
sasha: that kv_fetch_serial looks like the main offender. We used to have async kv prefetch for long queries. did that change?
ali: yeah the kernel change streamlined io paths and made kv fetch sync for fastpath. optimistic for short sequences but bad for long ones when cache misses spike.
chad: telemetry quick check: which tenants are most hit? can we filter by kv_hit_rate and seq_length?
meera: ran a quick query: `SELECT tenant, avg(seq_len), kv_hit_rate, p95(latency) FROM serving.spans WHERE time > now() - 1h GROUP BY tenant` — top 3 affected tenants have avg_seq_len >= 600 and kv_hit_rate < 0.6.
ryan: hypothesis: batch formation policy currently aggregates by earliest-arrival and kernel compatibility. short requests flood batcher, steal token budget, long sequences wait.
sasha: two quick mitigations we can try: 1) bump token_budget_target for seq_len>256, 2) re-enable async kv prefetch path for kernel_v2.4 for long lanes.
ali: agree. also propose admission tweak: when short/long mix > 70/30, prefer admit of one long per N shorts (config `long_slot_every_n=8`).
chad: experiment plan: A) increase token_budget by +30% for long lanes B) gate kernel_v2.4 fastpath for seq<=64 only C) enable async kv for lanes with predicted seq>256. run canary on a single pool.
meera: telemetry to collect: per-tenant p50/p95, kv_hit_rate, batch_size distribution, kernel_choice ratio, and token_budget_util. set retention 1h.
perf-bot: created experiment run: exp-3961234567 — canary pool `us-west-2-pool-5` applied with A,B,C. monitor channel #eng-monitoring.
ryan: small note: we should track cold-kv priming cost separately — warmup may spike short-term tokens. add a metric `kv_warmup_tokens` to the dashboard.
sasha: agreed. also let's add a microbenchmark: simulate 1000 short rps + 20 long rps and compare throughput/latency pre/post change. I can wire that up tomorrow.
ali: owners: meera (telemetry), sasha (bench), ryan (kernel gate PR), chad (canary), ill update runbook. next sync in 2h.
chad: thumbs-up. if canary shows improvement we'll roll config to all clusters with 10% rollout steps. :thumbsup:
meera: quick follow up: what SQL used for tenant selection so we can whitelist test tenants? `SELECT tenant FROM serving.metrics WHERE avg_seq_len > 400 AND kv_hit_rate < 0.65 LIMIT 10`
ali: saved. i'll kick off canary in 10m and post results.
perf-bot: canary started at 3961234589. will post summary in ~15m.
ali: thanks everyone — adding notes to the perf doc and will file a postmortem if regression persists.
ryan: if async kv reintroduces regression elsewhere we may need a kernel policy matrix keyed by (seq_len_bucket, kv_hit_prob, tenant_priority). but let's see canary first.
sasha: quick checklist added to the experiment: `- collect flamegraphs - collect kv latency heatmap - collect batch composition histograms - collect token_budget_util`
ali: perfect. ping me if you see outliers.
